results.expected_answer: There is no free seat. An Admin must free a seat, or the Owner must add seats or upgrade. The same invitation then works if it is less than 7 days old.

answer.answer: Support should explain that an Admin of the workspace must remove a member to free a seat, or the Owner must add seats or move to a larger plan. Once a seat is free, the same invitation link works again as long as it is less than 7 days old.

results.question: What happens, step by step, when a customer's card payment fails?
results.expected_answer: E-mail to the Owner and billing contact, retries after 1, 3 and 7 days, then a 21-day grace period (everything works), then read-only, then suspension at 60 days. Nothing is deleted.

answer.answer: When a payment fails, the workspace Owner and the billing contact receive an e-mail straight away. The card is retried automatically at specific intervals (such as 1 day, 3 days, and 7 days after the first attempt, or 3 days and 7 days depending on the document details). Updating the card before the next retry is usually enough to solve the problem, and no late fee is charged. If all retries fail, the workspace enters a grace period (either 14 or 21 days from the first failed attempt), during which everything keeps working and a banner reminds Admins of the overdue payment. After the grace period, the workspace becomes read-only (members can view dashboards but not edit them, scheduled reports are paused, and datasets stop refreshing). If the amount remains unpaid 60 days after the first failed attempt, the workspace is suspended and nobody can sign in until the payment succeeds.

results.question: Which plans include single sign-on, and how does an admin set it up?
results.expected_answer: Business and Enterprise. An Admin opens Settings → Security → Single sign-on, downloads the Kestrel SP metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, pastes the IdP metadata URL back, tests with one Admin, then enforces it.

answer.answer: Single sign-on (SAML) is included on the Business and Enterprise plans. To set it up, an Admin goes to Settings → Security → Single sign-on, downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, and then pastes the identity provider metadata URL back into Kestrel.

citations.label: C1
citations.quote: To set it up, an Admin opens Settings → Security → Single sign-on, downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, and pastes the identity provider metadata URL back into Kestrel.

results.question: I lost my phone and I can't log in anymore. What can I do?
results.expected_answer: Use a backup code. Without one, ask a workspace Admin to reset your second factor. If you are the only Admin or the Owner, contact support from the account's e-mail address; identity verification can take up to 2 business days.

answer.answer: If you lost your authenticator device and have backup codes, you can use one of your backup codes at the second-factor prompt, then set up two-factor authentication again from Profile → Security. If you have neither your authenticator device nor any backup code, you should ask an Admin of your workspace to reset your second factor from Settings → Members. If you are the only Admin or the workspace Owner, you must write to support from the e-mail address registered on your account.

results.question: Can I get a refund on my annual plan 45 days after it renewed?
results.expected_answer: Yes, under the current (March 2026) policy: annual plans are refundable within 60 days of renewal, pro-rated from the request date. The old 2025 policy allowed only 30 days.

answer.answer: Yes, annual plans can be refunded if the request is made within 60 days of the purchase or renewal date. Since 45 days is within this 60-day window, you can request a refund, which will be pro-rated for the unused full months of the annual period.

citations.label: C4
citations.quote: Annual plans can be refunded if the request is made within 60 days of the purchase or renewal date. The refund is pro-rated from the date of the request: you are refunded the unused full months of the annual period.
